--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_bipartite_node_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if a set of nodes is one side of a valid bipartition. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_bipartite_node_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if a set of nodes is one side of a valid bipartition. title: >- [Graph.is_bipartite_node_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Check if a set of nodes is one side of a valid bipartition. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes is one side of a valid bipartition. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25135-L25251){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_bipartite_node_set(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is bipartite node set](../assets/graphs/is-bipartite-node-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The path ann, party, bob, talk drawn in two rows, people on top and events below, with the candidate set outlined. Left: ann and bob form one whole side of the split, so is_bipartite_node_set returns True. Right: ann and talk are three hops apart along the accent path, so they sit on opposite sides; talk (accent) breaks the set and the call returns False." width="100%"} A bipartite graph can be 2-colored, and in each connected component the two colors are fixed up to swapping. This method checks that `nodes` takes exactly one color class in every component, so that it (and the remaining nodes) form a valid two-sided split. Use it to validate the "top" side passed to bipartite methods, especially on disconnected graphs where several splits are possible. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The candidate side, as IDs or labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every component's bipartition puts `nodes` entirely on one side (isolated nodes may go either way). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `nodes` repeats a node, a node does not exist, or the graph is not bipartite. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each component is 2-colored by breadth-first search and compared with `nodes`, in $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `bipartite.is_bipartite_node_set`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~bipartite_sets`) : The two sides of a bipartite graph. [](`~is_bipartite`) : Check whether the graph can be split into two sides. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each edge on its own can be split either way, so `A` can go with `C` or with `D`, but never with `B`: ::: {#a78a0dbd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("C", "D")]) sides = [["A", "C"], ["A", "D"], ["A", "B"]] [graph.is_bipartite_node_set(side) for side in sides] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [True, True, False] ``` ::: ::: ### Checking a side `davis_southern_women()` links 18 women in a town of the US South in the 1930s to the 14 social events (E1 to E14) each of them attended, and the `bipartite` attribute marks the two sides. The women form one side. Without Flora Price they don't, as she would then be on the same side as the events she attended: ::: {#02986f20 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} davis = ec.davis_southern_women() side = davis.get_node_attrs("bipartite") women = [n for n, s in side.items() if s == 0] flora = davis.get_id_from_label("Flora Price") others = [n for n in women if n != flora] davis.is_bipartite_node_set(women), davis.is_bipartite_node_set(others) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: E9 and E11 are the only events that Flora Price and Olivia Carleton attended: ::: {#e099b91f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} pair = ["Flora Price", "Olivia Carleton"] ties = [(w, e) for w in pair for e in ["E9", "E11"]] davis.layout_bipartite(nodes=women, aspect_ratio=0.5).plot( layout="pos", highlight=ties, label_by="label", height=900 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: With those two events gone, the two women are on their own, and either side will do for them: ::: {#cf11d56b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} davis.delete_node("E9").delete_node("E11") davis.is_bipartite_node_set(others) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: [Coloring, matching, and covering](../user-guide/coloring-matching.qmd#bipartite-graphs) splits the Southern Women network into its two sides with `bipartite_sets()`.
